scenario: AITA for demanding that my girlfriend (long distance relationship) takes the time to write me a message after she'd a very busy day? | My girlfriend and I live in a long distance relationship, as in several countries apart. She's at med school and currently in the practical part of her education. She has to work six days a week from morning till evening, including night shifts. Additionally, she has to prepare for very important exams very soon. The time she doesn't spend working, she spends studying or sleeping to recover. It gives us very little time to communicate, and communication is very important to me. She doesn't like the current situation, but she wants to do well in her education. I expect her to at least write me a message in the morning and the evening, just to hear something from her. It also eases my own mind, because if I don't hear anything I can stay at ease and have (for example) trouble sleeping. This is not because I am worried if I don't get messages, but because I get angry and I'm also a bit insecure. I think it should be possible for her to spend a minimum of one minute in the morning and the evening to write a few words. I normally, tend to write her regularly throughout her work days, just about thinks going on, but if she doesn't manage to write those one of those messages I just talked about, I'll stay silent until something comes from her. I also let her in an indirect/passive-aggressive way know that I am not happy with her lack of communication. Admittedly, part of my goal is to make her feel bad and to change her behaviour. I want to support her in any way possible through her difficult time, but I just can't help it if this minimum is not fulfilled. I know it pressures her and I feel bad, but I also feel the need to vent my frustration. She knows that it is important to me, but currently she has neither time or the energy to discuss it in length. I know she is trying, just as I am trying not to vent my frustration. Besides from that issue I have no problem with her being busy, I appreciate what she is doing and I let her know that. AITA for demanding that time from her and for being vocal about my frustration, even though I know she is trying?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being too demanding with my girlfriend. We're in a long-distance relationship, which is tough enough, but she's also really busy with her medical studies. She works six days a week, sometimes until late at night, and she's preparing for important exams. I get that she's super busy, but I really value our communication. I expect her to at least send a message in the morning and evening, just a few words. I know it's not much, but it helps me feel connected and less anxious. I usually message her throughout the day, just about random things, but if she doesn't respond in the morning or evening, I end up being silent and maybe even passive-aggressive. I admit that part of my goal is to make her feel bad so she changes her behavior. I want to support her, but I can't help feeling frustrated when she doesn't meet this minimum. I know it's pressuring her, and I feel bad about it, but I also need to vent my frustration. She knows communication is important to me, but right now she doesn't have the time or energy to discuss it in detail. I appreciate what she's doing, and I tell her that, but this one issue is causing tension. I'm wondering if I'm being too much to ask for these messages, especially considering how busy she is. I think about whether it's reasonable to ask for just a minute each morning and evening. It seems like a small thing, but maybe it's adding more stress to her already overloaded schedule. On the other hand, I need some reassurance that she's thinking about me, even if it's just a quick message. I don't want to come off as controlling, but I also don't want to feel neglected. I also consider how my passive-aggressive behavior might be affecting her. Maybe she feels guilty or pressured, which isn't fair because she's already doing so much. I want to support her, not make her feel worse. But I also need to take care of my own feelings and mental health. It's a tough balance. I wonder if there's a middle ground. Maybe we can find another way to stay connected without her having to send messages every day. Or perhaps we can set specific times when she can reach out, even if it's just a quick check-in. I also think about whether I'm being too rigid with my expectations. Maybe I need to be more flexible and understanding of her schedule, even if it means less communication. I also reflect on whether my frustration is more about my own insecurities and anxiety rather than her actions. Maybe I need to work on my own feelings of insecurity and find ways to cope without relying solely on her messages. That could involve talking to friends, engaging in hobbies, or maybe even seeking some support from a counselor. In the end, I'm trying to figure out if my demands are reasonable or if I'm being too hard on her. I want to maintain our relationship, but I also don't want to compromise my own well-being. It's a complicated situation, and I'm not sure what the best approach is.
